newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Ortiz sees no change in 1997 tax policy.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Ortiz sees no change in 1997 tax policy.

text.p: Mexican Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz said on Tuesday the Mexican government will neither seek to raise nor lower taxes in its 1997 budget.
"Frankly, I see it as being very difficult for us to propose a cut in tax rates (in the 1997 budget)," Ortiz said in a question and answer session in the Mexican Congress.
He said that the government aimed to finance increased social investment spending by cutting spending on public sector salary payments and other administrative expenses wherever possible.
Ortiz said the government's main tool for keeping its 1997 budget fairly balanced is improved tax collection.
"What we plan to work on, given that we're not going to propose higher taxes for next year, is improving administration of the tax system," he said.
The 1997 budget is due to be presented to Congress by November 15.
